StudyPlan.description: Represents a study plan tailored to a specific user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the progress report.

userId.description: Reference to the User this progress report belongs to. (Relationship: User 1:N ProgressReport)

studyPlanId.description: Reference to the StudyPlan this progress report is associated with. (Relationship: StudyPlan 1:N ProgressReport)

score.description: Score achieved by the user in a particular session.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support user authentication and the core entities of the AI Study Buddy application (Users, StudyPlans, and ProgressReports). It leverages path-based ownership for user-related data to ensure secure and efficient access control. Authorization independence is achieved through path-based ownership, eliminating the need for `get()` calls in security rules and enabling atomic operations.

*   `/users/{userId}`: Stores user profiles. This collection uses the User ID as the document ID, enabling straightforward user data retrieval and updates. Authentication is handled through Firebase Authentication, and the `userId` is obtained from `request.auth.uid`.
*   `/users/{userId}/studyPlans/{studyPlanId}`: Stores study plans owned by a specific user. This structure enforces ownership by placing study plans as subcollections under the respective user documents. The `userId` parameter ensures that only the authenticated user can access their own study plans.
*   `/users/{userId}/studyPlans/{studyPlanId}/progressReports/{progressReportId}`: Stores progress reports associated with a particular study plan. Nesting progress reports under study plans and users maintains a clear hierarchy and simplifies access control rules. Again, path-based ownership ensures only the user associated with the study plan can access the progress reports.
*   `/users/{userId}/cryptographyChatHistory/{messageId}`: Stores individual chat messages for the cryptography tutor feature. Nesting under the user ensures that a user can only access their own chat history, enforcing privacy and security.

This structure facilitates secure `list` operations because access to each collection is controlled by the `userId` in the path. A user can only list study plans and progress reports associated with their own user ID, preventing unauthorized access to other users' data.
